title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 40-45 of 156-4). Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, essentially combinatorial 'analysis situs', a tame-topology framework in the spirit of section 5 of the Esquisse d'un programme (1984). The ingredients are:
- a set M of 'multistructures' (strata or cells), with an order X' < X ('X' is a face of X');
- 'figures' F, which are sets of multistructures (F_X is the figure generated by X);
- a refinement relation Y << X (Y refines X);
- for each X, a 'shadow' X~ (a point-set or realization) and an 'open shadow / open stratum' X~°, meaning X~ minus the shadows of its proper faces.

Previous page (Cons. 8). For Y << X and a face X' < X, the Y' <= Y with Y' << X' form a subfigure R_{X'}, the refinement of X' induced by Y. It is the infimum of F_Y and F_{X'} for <<, and Y~ ∩ X'~ = ∪_{Y' in R_{X'}} Y'~. The corollary there: if no X1 with Y << X1 < X exists, then Y~° ⊂ X~°.

This page, first part (Corollary). If Y << X, then the open stratum of Y lies in the open stratum of some face of X. More generally, if F' is a refinement of a figure F, every open stratum of F' lies in a unique open stratum of F. Proof sketch: take the minimal face X1 <= X with Y << X1 and apply the previous corollary to X1. Uniqueness holds because the open strata of the faces of X partition X~. In modern terms this is the standard fact that a subdivision of a stratified, cell or regular CW complex refines the stratification: each open cell of the subdivision lies in exactly one open cell of the original.

This page, second part (a crossed-out 'Contre-ex.', then 'Je viens de m'apercevoir...'). Grothendieck finds a defect in his working definition of refinement ('F' refines F if each X' in F' refines some X in F', made explicit at the top of p. 45).
- In the model of pseudo-disks, take two disjoint loci x, y in the interior of a disk. Each is a degenerate ('infinitesimal') pseudo-disk refining the disk.
- So the figure {x, y} counts as a refinement of the disk.
- Yet it does not extend to a subdivision (here, a subdivision of the disk having x, y as nodes) inside his model.
- A bracketed NB recalls that the 'nodes' of a figure are its node multistrata, i.e. what a subdivision of a locus produces, F ∩ L.
Conclusion (finished on p. 45): it is inappropriate to call {x, y} a refinement. One should take SUBDIVISION as the primitive notion and define a refinement as a subfigure of a subdivision. This leads to the 'nouveau départ': a contrée is a triple (M, F, Σ) with Σ the relation 'F' subdivides F', subject to axioms C1 and C'1 and an order X <= Y iff X ∈ F_Y.

So the page serves the foundational problem of choosing primitives for a combinatorial tame topology. Its outcome is: subdivision is primitive, refinement is derived.
errors: The 'refinement' notion used up to this page (elementwise refinement) is too weak. As Grothendieck himself notes, it admits refinements, such as two interior points of a disk, that do not come from any subdivision. Results like Cons. 8 and the open-stratum corollary should therefore be read for refinements that are subfigures of subdivisions. This is the reason for the restart on p. 45.

The uniqueness claim ('une (unique) strate ouverte de F') needs the open strata of F to be pairwise disjoint. This presumably follows from axioms not visible here and is implicit, not proved on the page.

The exact nature of the obstruction in the pseudo-disk example (why {x, y} cannot be completed to a subdivision) is not legible or argued on the page. In ordinary PL topology, two interior points of a disk can be vertices of a subdivision, so the failure must be specific to his restricted model of pseudo-disks. The argument is therefore incomplete as written.

ideas.what: Each open stratum of a refinement lies in a unique open stratum of the refined figure.
ideas.modern_name: Subdivisions refine stratifications / cell decompositions (open-cell containment)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical PL topology and CW/stratification theory (Whitehead, Zeeman, etc.)

ideas.what: Taking subdivision rather than refinement as the primitive relation, with refinement defined as a subfigure of a subdivision.
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic subdivision structures; cf. abstract cell complexes, cofinal systems of subdivisions in PL and o-minimal cell decomposition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in PL topology; o-minimal axiomatics (van den Dries, Knight-Pillay-Steinhorn)
ideas.where_published: Programmatic hint only, in Esquisse d'un programme §5 (tame topology)

ideas.what: The 'contrée' (M, F, Σ): a combinatorial, pointless axiomatization of tame spaces via multistructures, figures and subdivisions.
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial/pointless tame topology; related to face posets of regular CW complexes and to locale-like approaches
ideas.usually_credited_to: No standard attribution for this specific formalism
ideas.where_published: Only the general program of tame topology is in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 attempt to axiomatize tame topology combinatorially ('contrées', with subdivision as the primitive relation, after a counterexample showing elementwise refinement is inadequate) is an unpublished foundational design choice. It is not reflected in the o-minimal or tame-topology literature, which starts from definable sets in a structure.
missed.quote: Je viens de m'apercevoir que dans le cas des pseudo-disques, deux lieux disjoints ... de l'intérieur ... Donc il est inapproprié
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Current attempts at synthetic or combinatorial foundations of stratified and tame spaces (exit-path categories, conically stratified spaces, poset-stratified spaces) face the same choice between refinement and subdivision as primitive. This is an early, explicit argument for subdivision-first axiomatics.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page is routine: open-cell containment for refinements, plus a self-correction of a definition. The interest is historical. It documents why Grothendieck's unpublished tame-topology axiomatics switches to subdivision as the primitive notion, which is a design detail absent from the literature but not a striking result.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'toute ombre[?] ouverte d'une strate eff.[?] Y' is more likely 'toute strate ouverte d'une strate eff. Y' (matching 'strate ouverte' used later on the page).
'deux lieux disjoints {+x,y+} Σ[?]' — the inserted symbol is the label x,y (possibly 'x,y ∈ Σ' or similar), not a separate Σ.
'comme un ensemble de connexité[?]' is doubtful. The context (p. 45) suggests 'comme un raffinement de ...' or similar.
'Les droites[?] des FF' in the NB is uncertain; it is possibly 'Les noeuds des F' or 'Les lieux des F'.
